comments.author: @zxwxz
comments.text: I believe that using LLMs to orchestrate agent workflows is a good idea. However, the main bottleneck currently lies in the limitations of LLMs themselves, rather than any flaws in the agent workflows. If GPT-5 can solve long-chain logical reasoning problems, or if designs like Q* can break through stalemates in fog-of-war scenarios, then we might see significant improvements. Otherwise, given the current capabilities of LLMs, they are likely to encounter obstacles in real-world situations.

comments.author: @c.d.osajotiamaraca3382
comments.text: You basically described a "Pareto Comparison Table"; where you assign a point system of needs: 1 being the lowest, and 5 = the critical need. Imagine you have 3 different model choices, and you want to grade them based on your chosen 5 quality asks. Define each quality and its value score. You then assign a quality agent to score all three proposed solution models against the maximum score of a yes/no for each quality ask. Then the agent would assess the score, summarize why one is better and then make recommendations for the lower scoring outcomes to make them better. This model can be used in daily life to increase the quality of judgement calls. Don't see why an agent wouldn't do so to exponential effect for each problem given. I love your work. Keep it up.
